newsitem.title: USA: Compaq CEO sees strong second half.
newsitem.headline: Compaq CEO sees strong second half.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp chairman and chief executive officer Eckhard Pfeiffer said Thursday the computer giant was "on course" for a strong second half, but said analysts were "getting ahead of themselves" in pushing up earnings estimates for the third quarter.
Pfeiffer told Reuters that the company's revamped product line was finding strong consumer acceptance, which was helping boost sales.
"The (new) products are very well accepted...consumer products are hot, so we're pretty much on course for a strong second half," he said after a speech to the Japan-U.S. Southern Conference here.
In July, Compaq executives said they were comfortable with third quarter earnings estimates of $1.03 per share, but those estimates as compiled by First Call have risen to $1.06 per share.
When asked if $1.06 was closer to what the company now expected, Pfeiffer said, "I cannot give you a statement on that, you know how it works. But they're getting ahead of themselves.
"There's a point when you say 'Listen, guys.' But we're in touch with them constantly," he said.
Compaq earned $0.96 per share, fully diluted, in the second quarter.
Pfeiffer also said that Compaq believes the market for memory chips is largely in balance in terms of supply and demand.
"We think it's pretty much in balance except for certain memory chips," he said.
